intro:
You track an engineering org reshuffle. Service ownership, team names and on-call duty change over time.

Initial specification:
- [e001] Agreed in the sync: the owning team of search-svc becomes `team-data`.
- [e002] Gus confirmed in writing that the owning team of billing-api changes to `team-edge`.
- [e003] Agreed in the sync: the owning team of media-proc becomes `team-infra`.
- [e004] Agreed in the sync: the owning team of audit-log becomes `team-edge`.
- [e005] Femi confirmed in writing that the owning team of mail-relay changes to `team-data`.
- [e006] After the review, the team settled on `team-infra` for the owning team of ledger-svc.
- [e007] Decision: the owning team of report-gen is now `team-data`.
- [e008] From now on, the dependencies of search-svc include `billing-api`.
- [e009] From now on, the dependencies of billing-api include `media-proc`.
- [e010] From now on, the dependencies of media-proc include `audit-log`.
- [e011] Wren added `billing-api` to the dependencies of report-gen.
- [e012] After the review, the team settled on `ana` for the on-call engineer for search-svc.
- [e013] Decision: the on-call engineer for billing-api is now `femi`.

Every event has a label of the form [eNNN] with a three-digit number. A higher number is later in time. A later event can change or cancel an earlier one.
Some material quotes old pages or copies for history. A quote of that kind is not a new statement.
